question: A 10-year-old boy from a low socioeconomic background presents with fever, migratory polyarthritis affecting the knees and ankles, and a new apical pansystolic murmur. Throat swab culture is negative, but anti-streptolysin O (ASO) titre is markedly elevated. According to the 2015 revised Jones Criteria, what is the MOST accurate diagnostic statement?

answers.text: ARF cannot be diagnosed without a positive throat culture for Group A Streptococcus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A positive throat culture is one evidence of preceding GAS infection, but it is not mandatory. Serological evidence — a raised or rising ASO titre or anti-DNase B — is sufficient to meet the 'evidence of preceding GAS infection' criterion. The Jones Criteria do not require a positive culture.

answers.text: The 2015 Jones Criteria require TWO major criteria, or ONE major plus TWO minor criteria, plus evidence of preceding GAS infection

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Per the 2015 AHA Jones Criteria revision: ARF is diagnosed by 2 major criteria, OR 1 major + 2 minor criteria, PLUS evidence of preceding GAS infection (positive culture/rapid test, OR raised ASO/anti-DNase B). This boy has 2 major criteria (carditis — new murmur, and polyarthritis) plus serological evidence — diagnosis is confirmed. The 2015 revision also introduced monoarthritis as a major criterion in high-prevalence settings.

answers.text: The presence of a murmur alone constitutes carditis as a major criterion only if confirmed by echocardiography

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Clinical carditis (new murmur, pericardial rub, cardiac enlargement or failure) counts as a major criterion even without echocardiography. However, the 2015 Jones Criteria introduced subclinical carditis (echocardiographic mitral/aortic regurgitation without audible murmur) as an additional major criterion — this expanded, not restricted, the clinical criterion.

answers.text: Sydenham chorea requires the concurrent presence of fever and arthritis to count as a major criterion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Sydenham chorea is a standalone major criterion for ARF — it can diagnose ARF even when fever has resolved and arthritis is absent, because chorea appears 1–6 months after the streptococcal infection. It does not require concurrent major or minor criteria.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the 2015 Jones Criteria structure. Two major OR one major plus two minor criteria are required, PLUS evidence of preceding GAS infection. Sydenham chorea is a standalone major criterion and throat culture is not mandatory — serology suffices.

Excellent. Memorise: 2 major OR 1 major + 2 minor + GAS evidence. Major criteria (CAJONES mnemonic): Carditis, Arthritis/polyarthritis (monoarthritis in high-prevalence settings), chorea, Erythema marginatum, Subcutaneous nodules.
